title: Enve Yosemite hike routes — source manifest
about: Ordered chains of NPS trail features (bundled trails.geojson ids = NPS NationalDatasets OBJECTIDs) that make up each published hike variant. `from`/`to` are fractions of a feature's arc length in travel order (from > to means the feature is walked against its digitised direction); {"at": anchor} trims at the nearest point of the feature to a named anchor. tools/build_hike_routes.py validates continuity and endpoints against the real geometry and writes the bundled pack.
derivation: Chains were produced by a shortest-path exploration over the NPS pack constrained to official map waypoints (docs/HIKING_ROUTE_AUDIT.md, docs/HIKING_UPGRADE_BRIEF.md), then reviewed segment by segment against the NPS trail maps (Vernal/Nevada, Yosemite Falls, Valley Loop, Cook's Meadow) on 2026-10-27. No connectors were invented; every segment is an NPS feature. Glacier Point Road additions (Taft Point, Panorama Trail, Pohono Trail) were found with tools/find_hike_chain.py over the same bundled NPS features and reviewed on 2026-10-30 against the NPS Glacier Point Road day-hike descriptions and the NPS wilderness trailheads map. Park-wide routes marked "geometry": "park" resolve against park-trails.geojson (all NPS_Public_Trails_Geographic features for YOSE, fetched 2026-10-30); they were found with tools/find_hike_chain.py over that pack, checked against relief-grid elevations and USGS NHD lake outlines where a destination has no NPS point, and reviewed on 2026-10-30 against the cited NPS regional day-hike pages.

routes.label: To the viewing area
routes.sequence: The paved western trail leaves the parking area and climbs gently to the viewing platform at the base of Bridalveil Fall, which drops 620 feet. Rocks above the platform are slippery even when dry; NPS says to stay on the pavement.
routes.traceNote: The NPS trail feature begins about 80 m east of the parking-lot point, so the short walk across the lot is not part of the mapped line. The published half mile is the NPS figure for the whole walk.

routes.label: Entire loop
routes.sequence: From stop 6 the paved loop runs clockwise: the eastern path, which is wheelchair accessible, leads north to the footbridge at the base of Lower Yosemite Fall, and the western path returns past the restrooms and drinking fountain. NPS suggests clockwise for the best views of the whole fall.
routes.traceNote: The mapped loop is close to the published mile; the few connecting metres at the shuttle stop are unnamed path and bike-path pieces.

routes.label: Entire loop
routes.sequence: From stop 6 cross Northside Drive onto the bike path and bear left to the Sentinel Bridge parking area. Walk out onto the bridge for the classic Half Dome view and back, then follow the boardwalk north across the meadow, over its two street crossings, and along the path beside Northside Drive to stop 6.
routes.traceNote: NPS describes the loop from the former Valley Visitor Center and says it can also begin at stop 6; this trace is the stop 6 version with the Sentinel Bridge out-and-back, so it is shorter than the published mile. The walk between the visitor center and stop 6 is access, not part of this loop. The separately named Sentinel Boardwalk south of the Merced is not on this route.

routes.label: Paved road to the lake and back
routes.sequence: A paved service road from shuttle stop 17 past the Tenaya Bridge junction to the end of the pavement at Mirror Lake. NPS defines the 2-mile round trip as the road end and back; vault toilets stand about halfway and at the end, and bicycles, strollers and leashed pets are allowed on this paved mile.
routes.traceNote: The mapped road is shorter than the published round trip; the published figure is the NPS estimate and the endpoint is the end of the pavement, as NPS defines it.

routes.label: Full loop around the lake
routes.sequence: Road to the lake, then the north-side trail along Tenaya Creek past the Snow Creek junction, across the two bridges over Snow Creek and Tenaya Creek, and back along the south side of Tenaya Canyon to the Tenaya Bridge junction and the road. NPS warns there is no safe crossing between the bridges and that the south side stays icy longest.
routes.traceNote: The mapped loop is a little under the published 5 miles and matches the Yosemite Guide's 4.5. Near the Snow Creek junction the NPS loop feature runs 16 m past the junction; the route is trimmed at the junction vertex itself.

routes.label: Half loop
routes.sequence: West from stop 6 on the bike path and Valley Loop Trail beneath the Three Brothers, past Camp 4 to El Capitan. Cross the Merced on El Capitan Bridge and return east on the south side past Cathedral Beach and the Four Mile trailhead to Sentinel Bridge, then north over Cook's Meadow to stop 6.
routes.traceNote: Traced from the NPS Valley Loop map and description (start at Lower Yosemite Fall, cross at El Capitan Bridge). The mapped loop is slightly longer than the 7.2 miles on the NPS trail page; the Valley hikes overview lists 6.5 miles for the half loop.

routes.label: Full loop
routes.sequence: The same start west to El Capitan, then on past El Capitan Meadow to Pohono Bridge at the western end of the Valley. Cross and return east on the south side past Bridalveil Meadow, Cathedral Rocks and the Four Mile trailhead to Sentinel Bridge, closing over Cook's Meadow to stop 6.
routes.traceNote: Traced from the NPS Valley Loop map (start at Lower Yosemite Fall, west end at Pohono Bridge, no eastern Valley extension). The mapped loop is slightly longer than the 11.5 miles on the NPS trail page; the overview lists 13 miles.

routes.label: Out and back on the John Muir Trail
routes.sequence: Cross the Happy Isles bridge and follow the paved John Muir Trail uphill beside the Merced. The footbridge, 0.8 miles up by the NPS count, gives the classic view of Vernal Fall; its drinking fountain and restrooms run May to October. Return the same way.
routes.traceNote: The mapped line is slightly longer than the published 0.8 miles each way; the trim ends exactly at the NPS footbridge point.

routes.label: Out and back on the Mist Trail
routes.sequence: Beyond the footbridge the Mist Trail splits left from the John Muir Trail and climbs its granite stairway of more than 600 steps beside the fall. Spray soaks the steps in spring and early summer. The railing at the brink of the 317-foot fall is the turnaround.
routes.traceNote: NPS maps no point for the brink, so the turnaround is the Mist Trail's nearest point to the NPS waterfall record. The mapped distance runs longer than the published 1.2 miles each way.

routes.label: Loop via Clark Point and the John Muir Trail
routes.sequence: Climb the Mist Trail to the top of Vernal Fall, continue past Emerald Pool to the next junction and take the cut-off up to Clark Point. Descend the John Muir Trail's longer switchbacks back to the fork above the footbridge. NPS suggests this loop to avoid descending the slick, crowded stairs.
routes.traceNote: The cut-off between Emerald Pool and Clark Point is an unnamed NPS trail feature. The mapped loop runs longer than the published 3.7 miles.

routes.label: Out and back on the Mist Trail
routes.sequence: Past the top of Vernal Fall the Mist Trail passes Emerald Pool and the Silver Apron footbridge, then climbs about 1.5 miles of rocky switchbacks beside the 594-foot Nevada Fall. At the top, bear right to the footbridge over the Merced above the fall, the turnaround.
routes.traceNote: The turnaround is the NPS footbridge point above Nevada Fall. The mapped distance is longer than the 5 miles in the Yosemite Guide and the 5.4 miles on the NPS trail page.

routes.label: Loop via Clark Point and the John Muir Trail
routes.sequence: Up the Mist Trail past both falls to the footbridge above Nevada Fall, then over the bridge onto the John Muir Trail. It descends past Clark Point with views of Liberty Cap and Nevada Fall and rejoins the fork above the Vernal Fall footbridge. NPS puts the John Muir Trail at about 4 miles down against the Mist Trail's 2.5.
routes.traceNote: The mapped loop runs longer than the published 5.8 miles.

routes.label: Columbia Rock
routes.sequence: From Camp 4 the trail starts its switchbacks at once through oak woodland. Columbia Rock, a mile and roughly 1,000 feet up, opens onto Yosemite Valley, Half Dome and Sentinel Rock. Return the same way.
routes.traceNote: The trim ends at the NPS Columbia Rock point, 0.2 m off the mapped trail.

routes.label: Top of Yosemite Falls
routes.sequence: Past Columbia Rock the trail dips briefly to the Upper Yosemite Fall viewpoint, then climbs steep, rocky switchbacks to the rim. At the top junction a short spur drops east to the overlook above the fall, the destination here. Yosemite Point and Eagle Peak are separate extensions NPS lists beyond it.
routes.traceNote: The destination is the end of the mapped overlook spur, about 0.3 miles past the junction where the named Yosemite Falls Trail feature ends, as the NPS map shows the route turning toward the brink. The mapped round trip is shorter than the published 7.2 miles.

routes.label: One way to Glacier Point
routes.sequence: A continuous steep grade from the base of Sentinel Rock to Glacier Point on an 1872 toll-trail alignment, with the Union Point side trip a little over two-thirds of the way up. The mapped trail ends at the Glacier Point trailhead beside the parking area and vault toilets.
routes.traceNote: The mapped line matches the published 4.8 miles; NPS notes the trail is now closer to five miles than four.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: Up the Four Mile Trail to Glacier Point and back the same way. NPS runs no free shuttle between Glacier Point and the Valley; summer tour buses drop off at Glacier Point but do not pick up.
routes.traceNote: The mapped line matches the published 9.6-mile round trip.

routes.label: Round trip from Mirror Lake Trailhead (stop 17)
routes.sequence: The paved Mirror Lake road, then the loop trail along Tenaya Creek to the Snow Creek junction about a mile beyond the lake. From there the Snow Creek Trail climbs out of Tenaya Canyon on dozens of switchbacks with Half Dome, the Quarter Domes and Clouds Rest in view, reaching the footbridge about 2.6 miles up. Return the same way.
routes.traceNote: The mapped round trip matches the published 9.4 miles, which NPS counts from the Mirror Lake trailhead to the footbridge.

routes.label: Round trip from Happy Isles
routes.sequence: Mist Trail to the top of Nevada Fall, then the John Muir Trail through Little Yosemite Valley, past the seasonal ranger station and composting toilet, to the Half Dome junction. The Half Dome Trail climbs the shoulder to the sub-dome steps and the cables; the mapped trail ends at the summit edge. Return the same way or by the John Muir Trail.
routes.traceNote: Two John Muir Trail features through Little Yosemite Valley (NPS ids 20072 and 22688) were added to the bundled pack for this route. The mapped trail ends about 75 m from the NPS Half Dome cliff point; the cables and sub-dome are not separate NPS features. The round trip matches the published 14 miles.

routes.label: Round trip via the John Muir Trail both ways
routes.sequence: The John Muir Trail the whole way: past Clark Point, over the footbridge above Nevada Fall, through Little Yosemite Valley to the Half Dome junction and up the Half Dome Trail. Longer but gentler than the Mist Trail stairs, and the route that stays open when the lower Mist Trail is closed in winter.
routes.traceNote: Same added features as the Mist Trail route. The round trip matches the published 16.4 miles.

routes.label: Round trip from the trailhead
routes.sequence: West from the trailhead through forest and meadow, joining the Pohono Trail near the rim to the Taft Point overlook. The way back is the climb.
routes.traceNote: The mapped line ends at the NPS Taft Point feature; the overlook itself is not a separate mapped feature.

routes.label: One way to Happy Isles via the Mist Trail
routes.sequence: Down from Glacier Point to the Illilouette Creek crossing, then the Panorama Trail's climb and traverse to the John Muir Trail above Nevada Fall, across the Nevada Fall footbridge and down the Mist Trail past Vernal Fall to Happy Isles. No shuttle returns you to Glacier Point.
routes.traceNote: NPS publishes 8.2 miles and says the final miles may follow either the John Muir Trail or the Mist Trail without saying which the figure measures; this trace uses the Mist Trail. The Mist Trail section closes for ice in winter.

routes.label: One way to Tunnel View
routes.sequence: The whole south rim of Yosemite Valley from Glacier Point west to the Wawona Tunnel: past Sentinel Dome and Taft Point and along the rim viewpoints including Dewey Point, then down to Tunnel View.
routes.traceNote: The trace follows NPS rim features from Glacier Point to the Tunnel View trailhead and matches the published 12.5 miles closely; side trips to individual viewpoints are not included.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: Gently downhill on the McGurk Meadow Trail through forest to the footbridge at the meadow; the climb is on the way back.
routes.traceNote: The mapped line ends at the McGurk Meadow footbridge, about 1.4 miles round trip against the published 1.6; NPS maps no point for the meadow or the historic cabin, so the turnaround is approximate.

routes.label: Round trip from the trailhead
routes.sequence: North from the trailhead through forest, then up the Sentinel Dome Trail across bare granite to the top.
routes.traceNote: The NPS Sentinel Dome Trail line climbs to within a few metres of the highest relief-grid sample on the dome, so the summit end is approximate. The final stretch is open rock; the line is orientation only.

routes.label: Round trip via McGurk Meadow
routes.sequence: Down the McGurk Meadow Trail across the meadow to the Pohono Trail, then west along the Valley rim to Dewey Point.
routes.traceNote: McGurk Meadow Trail features to the Pohono Trail junction, then the Pohono Trail to the point nearest NPS Dewey Point (about 30 m). The trace is within a few percent of the published 7.6 miles.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: Through forest and meadow on gentle grades, then a long, steeper climb to Ostrander Lake and the ski hut.
routes.traceNote: Five unnamed NPS trail features lead from the trailhead to the end of the mapped trail beside the lake, about 30 m from the NPS ski hut point. The trace matches the published 12 miles closely.

routes.label: Loop from the grove arrival area
routes.sequence: Along the Big Trees Loop and up the Mariposa Grove Trail past the Bachelor and Three Graces to the Grizzly Giant and California Tunnel Tree, then back down the Grizzly Giant Loop Trail along the edge of the grove.
routes.traceNote: Big Trees Loop, Mariposa Grove Trail and Grizzly Giant Loop Trail features, starting and ending about 8 m from the NPS trailhead point. NPS does not say which way round to walk; the trace runs anticlockwise up the main trail and returns on the loop trail.

routes.label: Round trip from the grove arrival area
routes.sequence: Up the Mariposa Grove Trail past the Grizzly Giant to the upper grove, around the Guardians loop past the fallen Wawona Tunnel Tree and the Mariposa Grove Cabin, then back down the same trail.
routes.traceNote: Drawn as one closed walk: the Mariposa Grove Trail up and back, plus the upper loop on Guardians of the Grove Loop Trail features (about 1.4 miles against the published 1.5). The mapped line starts about 30 m from the NPS trailhead point. NPS does not give a direction for the upper loop; it is drawn clockwise.

routes.label: Round trip to Wawona Point
routes.sequence: The whole Mariposa Grove Trail from the arrival area past the Grizzly Giant and through the upper grove to the end of the trail at Wawona Point.
routes.traceNote: Every segment is an NPS Mariposa Grove Trail feature; the mapped line starts about 30 m from the NPS trailhead point and its top end stands in for Wawona Point, which NPS does not map. The trace matches the newer published 7 miles; the older Wawona page's 7.75 miles is listed as a discrepancy.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: Up beside Chilnualna Creek, then switchbacks with views over Wawona, to the trail's closest approach to the falls.
routes.traceNote: Chilnualna Falls Trail features to the point nearest the NPS Chilnualna Falls point (about 40 m). The trace is about 7.1 miles round trip against the published 8.2.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: Across O'Shaughnessy Dam and through the tunnel, then along the north shore of the reservoir to the crossings below Wapama Falls.
routes.traceNote: Unnamed NPS trail features from the trailhead to the point of the trail nearest the NPS Wapama Falls point, which sits about 280 m upslope; the turnaround is approximate. The trace is within a few percent of the published 5 miles.

routes.label: Round trip from the trailhead beyond the entrance
routes.sequence: From the trailhead beyond the entrance, a long climb on unnamed trail to the Smith Peak Trail and up to the summit.
routes.traceNote: Unnamed NPS features to the Smith Peak Trail, whose end sits within 10 m of the highest relief-grid sample on the peak; the summit point is approximate. The trace is within a few percent of the published 13 miles.

routes.label: Round trip from the entrance station
routes.sequence: From the Hetch Hetchy Entrance, unnamed trail to the Cottonwood Meadow Trail, east past Cottonwood Meadow and up the Smith Peak Trail to the summit.
routes.traceNote: Starts at the NPS Mather Ranger Station trailhead point beside the entrance station, about 20 m from the first mapped feature; the first stretch is recorded by NPS as non-NPS trail. Unnamed features, the Cottonwood Meadow Trail and the Smith Peak Trail follow; the summit point is approximate. The trace matches the published 16 miles closely.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: Steeply down the Poopenaut Valley Trail to the Tuolumne River; the whole climb is on the way back.
routes.traceNote: One NPS feature, the Poopenaut Valley Trail, from the trailhead to its lower end by the river. Its 1.06 miles each way are about 15 percent short of the published 2.5-mile round trip; the relief grid gives the same 390 m drop NPS publishes.

routes.label: Round trip with the nature trail
routes.sequence: Down the old Tuolumne Grove Road into the grove, through the Dead Tunnel Tree and around the nature trail, then back up the road.
routes.traceNote: Drawn as one closed walk: Tuolumne Grove Road down and back, plus the Tunnel Tree Trail and the Tuolumne Grove Loop Trail in the grove (about 0.5 mile, matching the published half-mile nature trail). NPS gives no direction for the nature trail. The whole walk maps to about 2.7 miles against the published 2.5.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: Down the old Coulterville Road, keeping left where it forks, to the small Merced Grove.
routes.traceNote: One NPS feature, the Merced Grove Trail (Old Coulterville Road), to the point nearest the NPS Merced Grove point (about 18 m). In the NPS lines the left and right branches part at the trailhead itself, not half a mile in as the NPS page describes; the trace follows the left branch. About 2.8 miles round trip against the published 3.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: Up through forest and across granite slabs on the May Lake Trail to the lake.
routes.traceNote: One NPS feature, the May Lake Trail; its upper end, where the Mount Hoffman Trail begins about 100 m from the mapped shoreline, stands in for the lake. Close to the published 2.4 miles.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: From Tioga Road through forest and over a low saddle, down to the meadow at the south end of Lukens Lake.
routes.traceNote: The Lukens Lake Trail from the trailhead to the first point within 15 m of the mapped lake shore. That is about 1.8 miles round trip, a little over the published 1.6.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: East from White Wolf through forest, across the Middle Tuolumne River, then onto the Lukens Lake Trail to the north end of the lake.
routes.traceNote: Two unnamed NPS features and the Lukens Lake Trail to the first point within 15 m of the mapped lake shore. Close to the published 4.6 miles.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: From the Porcupine Creek trailhead across the creek and through forest and meadow on the North Dome Trail, down to the base of the dome and up to its top.
routes.traceNote: Unnamed features then the North Dome Trail; its south end lies within a few metres of the highest relief-grid sample on the dome, so the summit is approximate. About 9.2 miles round trip against the published 10.4.

routes.label: Out and back with the Lembert Dome side trip
routes.sequence: North from the Dog Lake parking area, up the Lembert Dome Trail to the top of the dome and back to the junction, on to Dog Lake, then back the same way.
routes.traceNote: Drawn as one closed walk because the Lembert Dome side trip and the Dog Lake leg are each walked twice; it maps to 3.8 miles, the published figure. The side trip ends at the NPS Lembert Dome point. Stay off domes in thunderstorms.

routes.label: Round trip
routes.sequence: From Dana Meadows southeast through forest and meadow, past the Spillway Lake junction, and up to Mono Pass on the park boundary.
routes.traceNote: Three unnamed NPS features from the trailhead to the point where the trail meets the park boundary and becomes a Forest Service trail; that point stands in for the pass. The trace matches the published 8 miles closely.

routes.label: Round trip to Glen Aulin
routes.sequence: West on the gravel road past Soda Springs, then the Pacific Crest Trail beside the Tuolumne River and down to the footbridge at Glen Aulin.
routes.traceNote: Pacific Crest Trail features throughout, ending at the north end of the Glen Aulin Bridge; NPS maps no point for Glen Aulin, so the destination is approximate. About 11.4 miles round trip against the published 11.
